parts.name: Left renal capsule
parts.info: A tough, thin fibrous coat around each kidney that protects it.
parts.fact: Hide the capsule to see the reddish cortex underneath.

parts.name: Left renal cortex
parts.info: The outer layer where about a million nephrons filter the blood.
parts.fact: The two kidneys together receive about a fifth of all the blood the heart pumps.

parts.name: Left renal columns
parts.info: Extensions of the cortex that dip between the pyramids and carry blood vessels.
parts.fact: They are also called the columns of Bertin.

parts.name: Left renal pyramids
parts.info: Cone-shaped parts of the medulla, packed with tubules that concentrate urine.
parts.fact: Each kidney has about 8 to 18 pyramids; this model has 9 or 10.

parts.name: Left renal papillae
parts.info: The tips of the pyramids, where urine drips out into the collecting cups (calyces).
parts.fact: Each papilla has around 20 tiny openings for urine.

parts.name: Left renal sinus
parts.info: The central space where the renal artery, vein and ureter enter or leave, cushioned by fat.
parts.fact: The renal pelvis, which funnels urine into the ureter, lies in the sinus.

parts.name: Renal arteries
parts.info: Branch straight off the aorta and bring about 1.2 litres of blood to the kidneys every minute.
parts.fact: The right renal artery is longer and passes behind the inferior vena cava.

parts.name: Renal veins
parts.info: Return filtered blood to the inferior vena cava.
parts.fact: The left renal vein is longer and crosses in front of the aorta.

parts.name: Abdominal aorta
parts.info: The main artery running down the back of the abdomen, giving off the renal arteries.
parts.fact: It splits into the two common iliac arteries near the belly button.

parts.name: Inferior vena cava
parts.info: The large vein carrying blood from the lower body back to the heart.
parts.fact: It lies to the right of the aorta.
